extractor.prompt: Stage 1 extraction, theme fundierung (founding of higher-order objectivities), one commentary.
extractor.note: Re-extracted with claude-opus-5. Replaces the 2026-09-11 pass, which took two units from the noema section and did not reach the section on sensible and categorial acts, where the founding doctrine of the Logical Investigations is treated directly.

coverage_note: Scanned 'The Intentionality of Sensible and Categorial Acts' (lines 143-168) and 'The Noema as Ideal Signification of a Judgment' (lines 261-294). The remaining 58 sections, including the chapters on time, hermeneutics and Derrida, are not covered.

units.term: Fundierung of categorial on sensible acts
units.claim: Heidegger summarizes the distinction between sensible and categorial intentional acts together with the relations of interdependence or founding that unite them.
units.quote: the distinction between different sorts of intentional acts, sensible and categorial, and the relations of interdependence or founding that unite them

units.claim: Neither Husserl nor Heidegger addresses the circularity that a categorial act cannot be defined without appeal to its being founded on a set of simple acts.
units.quote: a categorial act cannot be defined without appeal to its being composed of, or more precisely founded on, a set of simple acts

units.term: gestufte Akte governed by the logic of whole and parts
units.claim: Acts of synthesis are governed by the same logic of whole and parts that forms the real weave of the Logical Investigations.
units.quote: Such acts are governed by the same logic of whole and parts that forms the real weave of the *Logical Investigations*.

units.claim: Despite their rootedness in sensible perception, categorial acts never reduce to the simple acts that compose or found them.
units.quote: Despite their rootedness in sensible perception, categorial acts never reduce purely and simply to the simple acts that compose them or found them

units.term: the copula as founded categorial object
units.claim: The 'is' of a perceptual statement counts as a categorial object whose intuitive apprehension is founded on sensible perception without being reducible to it.
units.quote: a categorial object whose intuitive apprehension is founded on, but not reducible to, sensible perception

units.claim: Acts of ideation differ from acts of synthesis in excluding their sensible foundation rather than including it.
units.quote: differs from acts of synthesis precisely in excluding its sensible foundation rather than including it

units.term: categorial intuition as the foundation of language
units.claim: Husserl and Heidegger agree that categorial intuitions are not derived from language but constitute its intuitive foundation.
units.quote: far from being derived from language these categorial intuitions constitute its intuitive foundation

units.claim: That categorial acts constitute a new objecthood does not mean producing in the sense of manufacture but letting the being be seen in its objecthood.
units.quote: constituting does not mean producing in the sense of making and manufacturing, but letting the being be seen in its objecthood (*Gegenständlichkeit*).

units.claim: For Heidegger categorial objects are not objects of a higher order in a separate world of thought and are hardly genuine objects at all.
units.quote: Far from being objects of a higher order belonging to a separate world of thought governed by immutable laws, categorial objects for Heidegger are hardly genuine "objects" at all.

units.term: founding bond recast as condition of showing
units.claim: Under Aristotle's influence the bond between sensible and categorial is no longer strictly one of constitution but one between what shows itself straightaway and what makes that showing possible.
units.quote: That bond is no longer strictly a bond of constitution but a bond between what shows itself straightaway and what makes that showing possible.

units.term: synthesis of identification presupposed by identity
units.claim: The 1908 course already contains the decisive idea that consciousness of an identity presupposes a synthesis of identification.
units.quote: consciousness of an identity presupposes a synthesis of identification

units.term: implicit in the correlate, explicit only through synthesis
units.claim: The signified object stands as the identical signification does: implicit in the punctual noematic correlate but requiring a synthesis of identification to be grasped explicitly.
units.quote: The signified object is therefore in the same position as the identical signification itself: implicit in the punctual noematic correlate, but requiring a synthesis of identification to be grasped explicitly.

units.term: X as junction point or support of the predicates
units.claim: In Ideen I the X is the unifying centre and support of the predicates, to be distinguished from them yet incapable of being set apart and separated from them.
units.quote: the unifying centre, the junction point or support of the predicates, necessarily to be distinguished from them though it cannot be set apart and separated from them.

units.term: noema implying rather than being its sense
units.claim: Sense and object are bound to the noema inseparably, yet the punctual noematic correlate is not identical with the ideally identical sense but only implies it.
units.quote: sense and object are bound to the noema inseparably, but the punctual noematic correlate is not simply *identical with* the ideally identical sense — it only implies it, it "has" it;
